newsitem.title: UK: British Gas profits hit by charges.
newsitem.headline: British Gas profits hit by charges.

text.p: British Gas Plc reported higher nine-month operating profits on Thursday but said exceptional costs, including those for losses on gas purchase contracts, pushed it into heavy third-quarter losses at the bottom line.

British Gas took a charge of 294 million pounds on expected losses from contracts to buy and sell gas, helping to produce a third-quarter net loss of 364 million pounds. Operating profit for the first nine months rose by 105 million pounds to 835 million, helped by colder weather.

British Gas, currently undergoing a Monopolies and Mergers Commission inquiry into the regulatory price formula for its TransCo gas pipeline unit, said weak gas prices had increased losses in its industrial and commercial gas supply business. It said plans for demerger of TransCo remain on target.

The company said problems with new gas billing and customer service systems had slowed its cost reduction programme, and said these problems would require extra spending of 80 million pounds this year.

It said some 31,000 employees had left the company under its voluntary redundancy scheme by the end of the third quarter, a scheme launched in 1993, when Gas made a restructuring provision of 1.65 billion pounds ($2.77 billion). The company said it would review the need for further restructuring provisions at the end of the year.

Chairman Richard Giordano said in the results statement that the company was assessing the impact of Chancellor Kenneth Clarke's budget measure announced on Tuesday which cuts capital allowances on company assets with life expected to be longer than 25 years. He said the company would notify any resulting accounting adjustments in the fourth quarter. ($1=.5956 Pound)
